If you want an LLM-based method specifically for popularity prediction (and not just ranking), TRAIL is a fine-tuned LLM that jointly predicts short-term item popularity and generates explanations, using contrastive learning to align scores and explanations with structured trend signals. It’s designed for practical near-term popularity forecasting in recommendation settings where full-catalog per-user ranking is too time-consuming. [1]

If your goal is to recommend items while addressing popularity bias or improving fairness, FairLRM uses LLMs to semantically decompose popularity bias into item-side and user-side components using instruction-based prompts, and reports gains in both fairness and recommendation accuracy. [8]

If you instead want LLMs used to improve recommendation quality via re-ranking (with interpretability), the “LLM as Explainable Re-Ranker” approach combines traditional recommenders with an LLM-based two-stage training re-ranker that targets ranking metrics like NDCG. [2]
